overall_notes: The engineering scaffolding is strong: 3,909 passing tests, strict TypeScript, a provenance-checked deploy gate, a deadman watchdog, a clean sitemap/canonical setup, axe-clean event pages and a solid mobile ticket bar. The user-facing product is weaker than that machinery suggests. The three most important defects: (1) facts shown contradict the source and the page's own prose on headline slots: Kotsiras 'tonight' shown at the wrong Άλσος and on sale when it is at Nea Smyrni and sold out, and The Gathering listed on the wrong day at 'multiple venues' while the correct Lycabettus row is hard-stopped; (2) the A0 hard-stop removes about 40% of verified upcoming events (626 → 354), with date-conflict firing at 22.5% against its own 10% threshold, on top of already thin coverage (4 exhibitions, 5 events 'today'); (3) Greek pages carry English or missing descriptions (0 of 626 Greek descriptions, 35% with none), and legacy 'premium' prose with invented facts is still live. Measurement of the stated goal (AI citations and crawlers) is essentially empty. The live site is 34h stale because the deploy gate refused a dirty main tree, yet IndexNow and GSC were still pinged.
